predecessors.name: Habsburg Netherlands
predecessors.text: the northern provinces and the Flemish and Brabantine towns that signed the Union in 1579-1580, taken out of the Habsburg Netherlands then ruled for Philip II

successors.name: Dutch Republic
successors.text: the Union's land, now the independent United Provinces after the Act of Abjuration of 26 July 1581; Cliopatria's Dutch Republic row starts in 1582

ledger.x: 1579: Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht and the province of Groningen sign the Union of Utrecht on 23 January, in reaction to the Union of Arras.
1579: Ghent, Antwerp, Brussels and the Guelders quarters join the Union.
April 1580: Overijssel and Drenthe join, completing the Union's northern membership.
26 July 1581: the Act of Abjuration, 'a de facto declaration of independence from Spain', turns the rebel Union into the independent United Provinces.

wars.name: Eighty Years' War
wars.outcome: The Union of 1579 was the northern provinces' alliance against Spain; they declared independence in 1581 and Spain recognised the Dutch Republic by the Peace of Münster (30 January 1648).

certainty.note: A war-time alliance of provinces and towns: membership is by signature and changes month by month (January 1579, summer 1579, February and April 1580), and the front with the Spanish-held south is not a surveyed line.
